co_cecilville_slab_aka_cecil_rock.blurb: Cecilville Slab sits near Fremont Pass, on the Leadville side of the high country. It is a small, low-traffic slab with ten routes, mostly bolted single-pitch sport lines plus a couple of gear-protected ones. Grades run from 5.8 up to a single 5.10, with most lines at 5.8 and 5.9, which makes it a friendly place for climbers learning to lead or sharpening their skills. The surface is friction-oriented and can be a little dusty, with dirt patches on the left side. The walk from the car is very short. Sun reaches the face from around midday through late afternoon, and it is worth letting the rock dry after rain.

co_garden_the.blurb: The Garden is a small, secluded wall in Boulder Canyon, tucked into the middle of the north face of Tonnere Tower and screened from the road by big pines. It has ten routes, nearly all trad or mixed trad-and-bolt lines on granite, with a single top rope and one fully bolted line. Grades span 5.7 to 5.11, clustering in the 5.8 to 5.10 range, and the wall includes a pedestal and an exposed pinnacle. Being on the north side, it stays shaded for most of the day, which suits summer but leaves it cold late in the year. Expect a quiet setting rather than a crowded cliff.
co_garden_the.approach: Cross Boulder Creek, then follow the path that climbs up and to the left through the trees. Before the talus field, turn sharply right onto a level track heading upstream; the clearing at the wall lies a short way past a cluster of pines. It takes roughly five minutes from the crossing.

co_hillbilly_rock_1.blurb: Hillbilly Rock 1 is the lowest of the Hillbilly Rocks in Boulder Canyon, a short granite cliff of single-pitch lines about 35 to 50 feet tall. Of its ten routes, nine are sport and one is trad. Difficulty starts at 5.7 and 5.8 on the right, where the stone is weakest, and gets steadier and harder moving left, with a good block of 5.10s and 5.11s and a couple of 5.12s at the far end. The face is in shade in the morning. It suits climbers who want bolted pitches without a long hike, though the final scramble up the gully is steep.
co_hillbilly_rock_1.parking_note: Use the roadside pullout on the north side of the canyon road, a bit upstream of the Riviera, where the road widens into a passing lane.
co_hillbilly_rock_1.approach: From the pullout walk a few yards along the road, then follow a rough trail up the steep drainage above it. Expect poison ivy in the gully, especially on its right side. The bolts of the leftmost line show from the base.

co_kahuna_boulder.blurb: At Carter Lake, Kahuna Boulder is one sandstone block above the beach, a short way below the main northern bouldering. It holds ten problems, ranging from easy V2 and V3 lines up to some very hard V8, V9 and V11 projects, with plenty in the middle at V5 to V7. The standout feature is a clean, steep west face with excellent flat landings, and a big roof on one side. The face stays shaded through the morning and early afternoon. Lake level matters: the boulder sits partly under water for roughly half the year, so plan around the reservoir.

co_deville_3.blurb: Deville 3 is a detached buttress of roughly 400 feet on the north side of Twin Sisters, in the Deville Rocks group south of Estes Park. All ten routes here are trad, running from 5.7 through 5.11, with the bulk in the 5.8 to 5.10 range. The namesake two-pitch 5.7 is the area's popular classic, and several lines share ground with it. Some of the rock carries lichen and loose pieces, so test holds. The cliff gets sun well into late October and is at its best on crisp fall days or cool mornings. Descents are walk-offs.

co_between_the_bridges.blurb: Between the Bridges is a section of the Uncompahgre Gorge at the Ouray Ice Park, in the narrowest, darkest stretch of the canyon, so it sees little light. The ten ice routes here are mostly one pitch, around 80 to 150 feet, and skew steep and demanding: seven are WI5, with one each at WI3, WI4 and WI6. Many are protected with screws, and some lines mix in trad or bolts. Open water at the base can soak ropes and climbers, so bring spare layers. It is a place for confident ice leaders rather than beginners.
